definitions.explanation: The traditional name for the twelfth month. One of the most widely known of the old month names (和風月名). The kanji 師 (master, teacher) + 走 (run) reflect the folk etymology that even Buddhist priests are so busy at year-end that they run around. Still commonly used in modern Japanese, especially in seasonal greetings and media.

examples.japanese: {師走|しわす}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}り→入る：00494_hairu⟧、⟦{街|まち}→街：17306_machi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{慌|あわ}ただしく→慌ただしい：17686_awatadashii⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: December arrived and the streets became hectic.

examples.japanese: {師走|しわす}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{忘年会|ぼうねんかい}→忘年会：15800_bounenkai⟧や⟦クリスマス→クリスマス：03839_kurisumasu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{忙|いそが}しい→忙しい：00591_isogashii⟧。
examples.english: December is busy with year-end parties and Christmas.

examples.japanese: {師走|しわす}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{慌|あわ}ただしさ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧、⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦なかなか→なかなか：01547_nakanaka⟧⟦{取|と}れない→取れる：02376_toreru⟧。
examples.english: In the hectic rush of December, it's hard to find time to write New Year's cards.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The folk etymology is that {師|し} (Buddhist priests/teachers) ⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧ (run) because December is so busy with year-end Buddhist ceremonies. While this explanation is widely known, the true etymology is uncertain.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{師走|しわす} is one of the few traditional month names that remains in active everyday use. It evokes the particular busyness of December in Japan: ⟦{大掃除|おおそうじ}→大掃除：08347_oosouji⟧ (year-end cleaning), ⟦{忘年会|ぼうねんかい}→忘年会：15800_bounenkai⟧ (year-end parties), ⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧ (New Year's cards), and holiday preparations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {師走|しわす}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{忙|いそが}しさ (the busyness of December)
- {師走|しわす}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧ (to enter December)
- {師走|しわす}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{風物詩|ふうぶつし}→風物詩：08649_fuubutsushi⟧ (things characteristic of December)
